Subject: Geofencing exception request + DPIA evidence

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. ClearPath is planning a pilot that will keep a subset of EU patient data routed to a UK corporate cloud region for latency reasons. Legal has asked whether Redwood can support a narrow geofencing exception (EU origination -> UK region only) while we finalize an internal DPIA.

To move quickly they asked for: 1) written confirmation of the routing controls you can apply (per-route region pinning + fallback behavior), 2) a short DPIA evidence bundle (processing map + retention matrix + subprocessor list), and 3) whether Redwood can accept the UK addendum / IDTA with our minimal redlines.

Attached is our internal DPIA outline. Can your team provide the routing control doc and a proposed timeline for evidence handoff? We need this to present to our DPO by Friday.

Regards,
Sara
Senior PM, Integrations
ClearPath Health

High-level plan: 
• Today: confirm routing controls + list of what we will hand off for the DPIA evidence (processing map, subprocessor list, retention table, copy of SCCs/IDTA).

• Fri: internal legal to review your redlines; if there are substantive legal asks we loop in escalation.

I've attached a short routing control spec and our evidence inventory.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Geofencing exception request + DPIA evidence — IDTA considerations

Hi all,

Quick legal note from my side. We reviewed ClearPath's proposed redlines on the UK Addendum (IDTA). Two items likely require agreement conversations: 
1) Subprocessor egress: ClearPath requests contractual guarantees that subprocessor data will not be routed outside the UK/EU. Our current subprocessor map shows a US-based analytics processor (AnalyticsCo) used for anonymized metrics; we can add contractual commitments around pseudonymized metrics only, not raw payload.
2) Backup/escrow: ClearPath asks for a data escrow option for exports in case of vendor termination. Our standard playbook is an operational export window with certified transfer logs; offering escrow is a commercial exception and needs pricing + SOC/attestation steps.

We should propose a conservative IDTA redline set back to ClearPath that: a) limits subprocessor egress commitments to processed/anonymized telemetry and b) outlines an export/handback operational runbook (not full escrow) with transfer logs and a 30-day notice SLA.

I recommend we include a short technical appendix that explains automatic prefix caching, route pinning logic (per-route tags), and our KV cache eviction that preserves no PII in metrics pipelines. Hannah — can you validate the technical appendix and confirm the AnalyticsCo behavior?

—Kimberly
Sr. Counsel (Privacy)
From: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@clearpath.health>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@clearpath.health, Anna Berg <anna@berg-legal.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Geofencing exception request + DPIA evidence — IDTA considerations

Kimberly — thanks, that framing helps. A couple clarifications from our side: 
• AnalyticsCo only receives anonymized metrics, but our DPO still wants a written guarantee (not necessarily escrow) that raw PII is never copied to that pipeline.
• For the export/handback runbook, our procurement prefers something documented we can include in the DPIA appendix (runbook + transfer logs sample + agreed SLAs).

We can accept an operational export with certified logs if Redwood provides the template and a sample transfer log format. If pricing for escrow is required we can put that in procurement as a separate commercial ask.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood would accept a temporary canary period (UK-only routing for 30 days) after which we will switch to EU routing unless our DPIA outcome requires continuing UK routing. That would help our security team validate latency impact.

Thanks,
Sara
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@clearpath.health>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Geofencing exception request + DPIA evidence and routing plan

Hi Sara — following up from legal. We can provide: 
1) A signed routing controls statement (per-route region pinning + explicit fallback to EU regions with circuit-breaker),
2) An evidence bundle (processing map, retention matrix, subprocessor list) by EOD Wednesday (we will include sample transfer logs), and
3) Acceptance of your IDTA redlines with the clarifications Kim flagged — we will propose language that limits subprocessor egress guarantees to anonymized telemetry and replaces escrow with the operational export runbook.

Regarding the canary: Redwood is comfortable with a 30-day UK-only canary. During that time we will enable verbose transfer logs and a temporary audit hook for ClearPath's security team. If after 30 days your DPIA requires continuation of UK routing, we'll treat that as a contractual amendment and scope an SLA/price if needed.

I'll attach the redline (IDTA_redline_v3.docx) and a short appendix that shows sample transfer log entries. Hannah, Kim — can you review the proposed appendix and confirm the telemetry guarantee language before I send to ClearPath?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Thanks everyone — quick operational confirmations: 
• AnalyticsCo: we run anonymization at the edge; no raw payload leaves Redwood for analytics. I'll attach our anonymization spec to the evidence bundle.
• Routing controls appendix: confirmed — per-route tags + explicit fallback policy + circuit-breaker thresholds (60s error spike or sustained 10% target-region capacity loss).
• Logs: sample transfer logs included; format is JSONL with transaction_id, timestamp, source_region, target_region, route_tag, bytes_transferred, operator_id.

I will upload the packaged evidence (DPIA_summary_v1.pdf, processing_map_q3.csv, anonymization_spec.txt, IDTA_redline_v3.docx) to the Drive link and send to you once complete. Planning the evidence handoff by 2026-09-15 18:00 UTC.
